findings.title: Ec2 Imdsv1 Optional
findings.description: The current configuration has http_tokens set to 'optional', which allows IMDSv1 and makes the instance vulnerable to SSRF attacks. Enforcing IMDSv2 by setting http_tokens to 'required' ensures that only IMDSv2 is used, mitigating the vulnerability. This change prevents the instance from using the less secure IMDSv1 protocol.
findings.fix_hint: Update the http_tokens value to 'required' to enforce IMDSv2

findings.title: Xentinel Hardcoded Aws Access Key
findings.description: Hardcoding sensitive credentials like AWS access keys and database passwords poses a significant security risk, as they can be exposed to unauthorized parties. Using environment variables to store these credentials helps to keep them secure and separate from the codebase. This approach also makes it easier to manage and rotate credentials without modifying the code.
findings.fix_hint: Use environment variables to store sensitive credentials
findings.fixed_code:
AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID = os.environ['AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID']
AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY = os.environ['AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY']
DB_PASSWORD = os.environ['DB_PASSWORD']
STRIPE_SECRET = os.environ['STRIPE_SECRET']

findings.title: Xentinel Hardcoded Aws Secret
findings.description: Hardcoding AWS secret access keys poses a significant security risk as it can lead to unauthorized access to AWS resources. Using environment variables to store sensitive credentials is a more secure approach. This way, sensitive information is not committed to the codebase and can be managed securely outside of the application.
findings.fix_hint: Use environment variables to store sensitive credentials like AWS access keys

findings.title: Tainted Sql String
findings.description: The original code is vulnerable to SQL injection because it directly inserts user input into the query string. By using a parameterized query, the database driver will properly escape the input, preventing malicious SQL from being executed. This fix replaces the vulnerable line with a parameterized query, passing the user_id as a separate parameter to the execute method.
findings.cwe: CWE-704: Incorrect Type Conversion or Cast
findings.fix_hint: Use parameterized queries to prevent SQL injection attacks
findings.fixed_code: query = "SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ?"; result = conn.execute(query, (user_id,)).fetchall()

findings.title: Subprocess Injection
findings.description: The original code is vulnerable to command injection because it uses the shell=True argument and passes the command as a string, allowing an attacker to inject malicious commands. By passing the command and arguments as a list, we avoid the shell injection vulnerability. The fixed code uses the subprocess.check_output function with a list of arguments to safely execute the ping command.
findings.cwe: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')
findings.fix_hint: Use the subprocess module with a dictionary to allowlist a set of commands and avoid shell injection by passing arguments as a list instead of a string

findings.title: Dangerous Subprocess Use
findings.description: The original code is vulnerable to command injection because it directly uses user-controlled input in the subprocess function. Using shlex.quote() to escape the input ensures that it is treated as a literal string, preventing malicious actors from injecting arbitrary commands. This fix assumes that the shlex library is imported with 'import shlex'
findings.cwe: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')
findings.fix_hint: Use the shlex library to escape user-controlled input for the subprocess function

findings.title: Subprocess Shell True
findings.description: The original code uses shell=True, which can lead to command injection attacks. By passing the command and arguments as a list, we avoid the shell and prevent injection vulnerabilities. This fix ensures that only the intended ping command is executed, without allowing arbitrary shell commands.
findings.cwe: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')
findings.fix_hint: Replace the subprocess call with a safer alternative that avoids shell injection vulnerabilities

findings.title: Path Traversal Open
findings.description: The vulnerability is caused by directly using user-provided input in the filename, allowing an attacker to traverse the file system. To fix this, we need to validate and sanitize the filename by removing any directory traversal characters. This prevents an attacker from accessing sensitive files outside the intended directory.
findings.cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')
findings.fix_hint: Validate and sanitize the filename to prevent path traversal attacks
findings.fixed_code: filename = request.args.get('name'); filename = filename.replace('../', '').replace('..\', ''); filename = '/var/data/' + filename; with open(filename) as f: return f.read()

findings.title: Xentinel Sql Injection Format
findings.description: The original code is vulnerable to SQL injection because it directly interpolates user input into the query string. Using parameterized queries with the '?' placeholder and passing the user input as an array to the query method prevents the input from being executed as SQL code. This fix ensures that the input is treated as literal input, not as part of the SQL command.
findings.fix_hint: Use parameterized queries to prevent SQL injection
findings.fixed_code: const query = 'SELECT * FROM users WHERE username = ? AND password = ?'; conn.query(query, [username, password], (err, results) => { callback(results && results.length > 0); });

findings.title: Security group allows unrestricted RDP (port 3389)
findings.description: The current security group rule allows unrestricted access to RDP on port 3389, which is a critical security risk. To fix this, we need to restrict the access to a specific IP address or range. The provided fixed code snippet updates the security group rule to only allow RDP access from the specified IP range.
findings.fix_hint: Restrict the security group rule to only allow RDP access from a specific IP address or range
findings.fixed_code: aws_security_group_rule.app_sg_rule { source_cidr_blocks = ["192.168.1.0/24"] type = "ingress" from_port = 3389 to_port = 3389 protocol = "tcp" security_group_id = aws_security_group.app_sg.id }

findings.title: Security group allows unrestricted SSH (port 22)
findings.description: The current security group rule allows unrestricted access to port 22, which is a critical security risk. To fix this, update the security group rule to only allow SSH access from a trusted IP address. Replace "your_trusted_ip" with the actual IP address that requires SSH access.
findings.fix_hint: Restrict the source IP address for SSH access in the security group rule
findings.fixed_code: aws_security_group_rule.app_sg_ssh { type = "ingress" from_port = 22 to_port = 22 protocol = "tcp" cidr_blocks = ["your_trusted_ip/32"] }

findings.title: RDS instance publicly accessible
findings.description: The RDS instance is currently publicly accessible, which is a critical security risk. To fix this, the 'publicly_accessible' attribute should be set to false to restrict access to the instance. This change will prevent the instance from being accessible over the internet.
findings.fix_hint: Set the 'publicly_accessible' attribute to false for the RDS instance

findings.title: S3 bucket allows public ACL
findings.description: The current configuration allows public access to the S3 bucket, which is a critical security risk. Setting the ACL to private restricts access to only authorized users. This change should be applied to the aws_s3_bucket resource in the main.tf file.
findings.fix_hint: Set the ACL of the S3 bucket to private to prevent public access

findings.title: S3 bucket allows public ACL
findings.description: TERRAFORM check CKV_AWS_20 failed on resource 'AWS::S3::Bucket.AppBucket'.
findings.fix_hint: Set the ACL of the S3 bucket to private to prevent public access

findings.title: S3 Block Public Access not enabled
findings.description: The S3 Block Public Access feature must be enabled to prevent unauthorized access to the bucket. This can be achieved by adding the block_public_access configuration to the AppBucket resource. By setting block_public_acls, block_public_policy, ignore_public_acls, and restrict_public_buckets to true, public access to the bucket is effectively blocked.
findings.fix_hint: Enable S3 Block Public Access on the AppBucket resource

findings.title: S3 bucket allows public policy
findings.description: The current S3 bucket policy allows public access, which is a critical security risk. To fix this, we need to update the policy to deny all public access. This can be achieved by adding a bucket policy that explicitly denies any S3 actions for all principals.
findings.fix_hint: Update the S3 bucket policy to restrict public access

findings.title: IAM policy allows wildcard resource (*)
findings.description: The current IAM policy allows access to all resources using a wildcard (*), which is a security risk. To fix this, the policy should be updated to specify explicit resources, such as the ARN of a specific EC2 instance. This will ensure that the policy only grants access to the intended resources.
findings.fix_hint: Update the IAM policy to specify explicit resources instead of using a wildcard (*)

findings.title: Admin Managed Policy: AdministratorAccess
findings.description: The current policy grants unrestricted AWS access, violating the principle of least privilege. A custom policy should be created that only grants the necessary permissions for the AppLambdaRole and DeployUser, such as lambda execution and S3 access. This will prevent over-privileged access and reduce the risk of security breaches.
findings.fix_hint: Replace the AdministratorAccess policy with a custom policy that grants only the necessary permissions for the AppLambdaRole and DeployUser

findings.title: Dangerous IAM action: iam:*
findings.description: The current policy grants full IAM control, which is a critical security risk. To fix this, we need to replace the 'iam:*' action with specific required actions, such as 'iam:CreateRole' and 'iam:AttachRolePolicy', to limit the privileges. This change ensures that the policy only allows necessary actions, reducing the attack surface.
findings.fix_hint: Replace the 'iam:*' action with specific required actions in the AppInlinePolicy

findings.title: Privilege Escalation Path Detected
findings.description: The original policy allows the DeployUser to create a Lambda function with any role, which is a privilege escalation path. The fixed policy restricts the DeployUser to only create Lambda functions and pass the AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole, which is a more limited and secure set of permissions. This change prevents the DeployUser from creating a Lambda function with an admin role, mitigating the privilege escalation vulnerability.
findings.fix_hint: Restrict the AppInlinePolicy to only allow necessary actions and resources

findings.title: Dangerous IAM action: *
findings.description: The current policy grants all AWS permissions to all resources, which is a critical security risk. To fix this, we need to specify the exact actions required by the lambda function, such as logging permissions. By replacing the wildcard action with a specific set of actions, we can significantly reduce the attack surface.
findings.fix_hint: Replace the wildcard action with a specific set of actions required by the lambda function

findings.title: Admin Policy Reference: AdministratorAccess
findings.description: The AdministratorAccess policy grants full AWS access, which is a security risk. A custom policy should be created to grant only the necessary permissions for the lambda execution role, such as logging permissions. This fix replaces the AdministratorAccess policy with a custom policy that grants only the necessary logging permissions.
findings.fix_hint: Replace the AdministratorAccess policy with a custom policy that grants only the necessary permissions for the lambda execution role

findings.title: Aws Db Instance No Logging
findings.description: The RDS instance is missing logging configuration, which can cause important event information to be lost. Enabling logging will allow for better monitoring and debugging of the database instance. The enabled_cloudwatch_logs_exports parameter should be set to include the desired log types, such as error-log, general-log, and slowquery-log.
findings.cwe: CWE-311: Missing Encryption of Sensitive Data
findings.fix_hint: Enable logging for the RDS instance by setting the enabled_cloudwatch_logs_exports parameter

findings.title: Rds Insecure Password Storage In Source Code
findings.description: The hardcoded password in the source code is a security risk as it can be accessed by unauthorized users. Using the random_password resource generates a random password at runtime, reducing the risk of password exposure. The aws_db_instance_password resource can be used to generate a random password for the RDS instance.
findings.fix_hint: Use the random_password resource to generate a random password for the RDS instance

findings.title: Aws Ec2 Has Public Ip
findings.description: The EC2 instance has a public IP address assigned due to the associate_public_ip_address being set to true, which poses a security risk. Setting it to false will prevent public IP address assignment, blocking public access to the instance. This change will help mitigate potential attacks and reduce the instance's attack surface.
findings.cwe: CWE-1220: Insufficient Granularity of Access Control
findings.fix_hint: Set associate_public_ip_address to false to prevent public IP address assignment

findings.title: Sql Injection Db Cursor Execute
findings.description: The original code is vulnerable to SQL injection because it directly inserts user input into the query string. By using parameterized queries, the input is treated as a literal value, preventing an attacker from injecting malicious SQL. The corrected code uses the `?` placeholder and passes the `user_id` as a separate argument to `execute()`

findings.title: Avoid_App_Run_With_Bad_Host
findings.description: The current code runs the Flask app on all available network interfaces, making it publicly accessible. To fix this, we should bind the app to a specific IP address, such as localhost (127.0.0.1), to restrict access. Additionally, debug mode should be disabled in production to prevent exposure of sensitive information through full stack traces.
findings.cwe: CWE-668: Exposure of Resource to Wrong Sphere
findings.fix_hint: Change the host parameter in the app.run function to a specific IP address or localhost to prevent public exposure

findings.title: Debug Enabled
findings.description: The debug flag in Flask should be disabled in production to prevent sensitive information leaks. Setting debug to False will prevent full stack traces from being exposed. Environment variables can also be used to configure the debug flag for more flexibility.
findings.fix_hint: Set the debug flag to False or configure it using environment variables

findings.title: Direct Response Write
findings.description: The original code directly writes user input to the response, bypassing HTML escaping and exposing the application to XSS attacks. To fix this, we use a template engine like EJS or Pug to render the HTML and automatically escape user input. This ensures that any user-provided data is safely escaped and cannot be executed as code.
findings.cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')
findings.fix_hint: Use template engine to render HTML and escape user input
findings.fixed_code: function renderProfile(req, res) { const name = req.query.name; res.render('profile', { name: name }); }

findings.title: Raw Html Format
findings.description: The original code directly interpolates user input into the HTML response, making it vulnerable to XSS attacks. To fix this, we use DOMPurify to sanitize the user-provided input, preventing any malicious code from being executed. This ensures that only safe and expected content is rendered in the HTML response.
findings.cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')
findings.fix_hint: Use a templating engine or a sanitization library like DOMPurify to prevent XSS vulnerabilities

findings.title: Security group unrestricted ingress
findings.description: The security group 'app_sg' has an unrestricted ingress rule, allowing traffic from any IP address. To fix this, we need to restrict the ingress to specific IP addresses or security groups. The provided fixed code snippet restricts ingress to the IP range '10.0.0.0/16' for SSH traffic on port 22.
findings.fix_hint: Restrict ingress to specific IP addresses or security groups
findings.fixed_code: resource "aws_security_group" "app_sg" { ingress { from_port = 22 to_port = 22 protocol = "tcp" cidr_blocks = ["10.0.0.0/16"] } }

attack_chains.title: Cloud Infrastructure Takeover
attack_chains.description: An attacker gains access to the cloud infrastructure by exploiting hardcoded AWS credentials in the code, then uses the security group rules to access the RDS instance and exfiltrate sensitive data.
steps: Step 1: attacker reads hardcoded AWS access key and secret in xentinel-demo-repo/src/app.py using finding 6ff9f975 and caa7a80d
Step 2: this gives them access to the cloud infrastructure, where they can use finding 236ccbb5 to access the RDS instance via unrestricted RDP
attack_chains.remediation: Remove hardcoded AWS access key and secret from xentinel-demo-repo/src/app.py

attack_chains.title: Privilege Escalation and Data Exfiltration
attack_chains.description: An attacker escalates privileges using a dangerous IAM action, then uses the elevated privileges to exfiltrate sensitive data from the S3 bucket.
steps: Step 1: attacker exploits finding 5dedd3be to escalate privileges using a dangerous IAM action
Step 2: this gives them access to the S3 bucket, where they can use finding de03de08 to exfiltrate sensitive data
attack_chains.remediation: Remove the dangerous IAM action from the policy

attack_chains.title: Code Execution and RDS Access
attack_chains.description: An attacker gains code execution using a subprocess injection vulnerability, then uses the code execution to access the RDS instance and exfiltrate sensitive data.
steps: Step 1: attacker exploits finding d383d2df to gain code execution via subprocess injection
Step 2: this gives them access to the RDS instance, where they can use finding 0d85fdd7 to exfiltrate sensitive data
attack_chains.remediation: Fix the subprocess injection vulnerability in xentinel-demo-repo/src/app.py
